brief: Morgan Stanley's weekly Global Reflections argues the S&P 500's calm surface masks a weaker market beneath it. Realized vol sits at the 14th percentile even as the Russell 2000 has fallen five straight weeks and 54% of Russell 3000 names carry drawdowns over 20% since June. Just 10 stocks drive 68% of Q3 earnings growth against a 29.5% consensus EPS headline, making earnings season the test of whether gains broaden. US banks have fallen 13% since August with a 14-day RSI of 27, the widest oversold gap versus the S&P since 1993, though MS still likes banks into 2027. Credit shows the same split: CCC spreads have closed above 1,000bp, a record ratio to broader high yield that MS calls its most sobering data point and says has historically preceded a worse credit cycle, as AI debt issuance crowds out weaker borrowers. Treasury yields hit 5.30%, the highest since 2002, and MS still expects two more 25bp hikes despite a weak September payrolls print. Hedge funds net sold AI infrastructure this week even as MS frames a 34% power shortfall through 2028 as the hyperscaler bull case, pushing behind-the-meter power as the structural fix.
